decisions.question: Your card offered a hand-held as a far-end radio for the world map's radio coverage picture. I left it out and offered a relay mast and a relay post in its place. Keep it out?
decisions.context: Built in Radio Framework 0.42.0 (row 700). No call between tiles uses a hand-held today: a hand-held reaches a vehicle on its own map, and the vehicle reaches home. The radio's rule is that a figure the interface shows must change an outcome somewhere, so a hand-held picture would show reach nothing uses.

options.label: Keep it out
options.detail: As built: vehicle radio, vehicle radio with its mast up, relay mast, relay post, vehicle by Morse

options.label: Make it real
options.detail: Let a caravan on foot with hand-helds call home between tiles (a new behaviour, about 12 tiles of reach on flat ground), then add the hand-held picture

options.label: Add the picture anyway
options.detail: A hand-held button whose picture is labelled as showing reach no call uses yet

decisions.why: It keeps every picture honest; making it real is a fair second choice if caravans on foot should have radio too

decisions.question: The world map's radio coverage pictures are built but their cost is not measured. Record it on your colony when you first try them?
decisions.context: Radio Framework 0.42.0 and 0.43.0 (rows 700 and 701). The radio's rules say anything that draws or recomputes is recorded with scripts/perf.py before and after, on your colony, asking first. By design it costs nothing while off and at most 1.5 ms a frame while a picture is being worked out. A recording can hitch the game, so save first.

options.label: Yes, record it
options.detail: Say go with the world map up: one recording with the picture off, one while it is being worked out, one once shown

options.label: Not now
options.detail: The design record keeps saying 'not measured'; try the pictures by feel first

decisions.why: Your screenshot showed 11 FPS on the colony map, and the radio's first concern is performance: measured, never assumed
